title: Meaning of the input clause group
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with a binary code for its optional states. For natural numbers $m,t$, an assignment $a:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$, and a Boolean word $y$ of length $m$, suppose $a(j)=y_j$ for every $j<m$. Then the input clause group at time $t$ evaluates to true under $a$ if and only if the input slice of the raw block at time $t$ equals the two-bit code of the symbol of $y$ read at the machine's input-head position at time $t$, with blank symbols at the boundary positions.
replaced: Let $y$ be a word of length $m$ and let the assignment $a$ agree with $y$ on the first $m$ variables. Then the input clause group at time $t$ evaluates to true under $a$ exactly when the input slice of the raw block at $t$ encodes the input symbol of $y$ at the oblivious input position of time $t$.
